summary: This roadmap extends automorphic bundles from sections to integral coherent cohomology, finite equivariant perfect models and derived Hecke actions. It connects those constructions to canonical, interior and cuspidal automorphic comparisons, with explicit Siegel weight ranges and normalizations. Boundary localization is separated into the all-degree rational Siegel case and the degree-zero totally real case. Multiplicity and classification assumptions remain visible in the final cuspidal descriptions and dimension formula.

nodes.title: The integral de Rham Levi torsor
nodes.statement: On a supplied toroidal Siegel model over O with finite locally free logarithmic Hodge factors and its polarized degenerating abelian family and logarithmic Hodge sequence, let M_dR be the torsor of triples (ψ₁,ψ₂,c), with ψ₁:O^g≃Lie(A), ψ₂:O^g≃ω_(Aᵗ), c a unit, and ψ₂=c(ψ₁ᵗ)⁻¹ after the polarization identifies the Hodge factors. It is a right torsor under the Siegel Levi M≃GL_g×G_m. The family, its dual and polarization are the extensions supplied by the compactification model; arbitrary semi-abelian schemes are not asserted to admit this datum.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Use the extended logarithmic Hodge sequence and polarization from C4–C5 and the deep-level models from C13.
Trivialize Lie(A) locally and construct ψ₂ from ψ₁ and c; verify the Levi change-of-frame law.
Identify the generic fibre with the parent principal bundle reduced to its Hodge Levi.
acceptance: Compare both Hodge factors, including the multiplier, on an ordinary split chart.

nodes.title: Integral dual-Weyl automorphic coefficients
nodes.statement: For a dominant Levi weight κ and an integral dual-Weyl module V_κ imported from LP3, define ω^κ=M_dR×^M V_κ using B0’s associated-bundle functor. With right B-equivariance f(mb)=(w₀,Mκ)(b⁻¹)f(m), left translation is (m′f)(m)=f(m′⁻¹m). Thus ω^κ is π_*O_(M_dR)[−w₀,Mκ], with this action. Use its canonical and boundary-ideal subcanonical extensions on the supplied integral model; do not replace an integral dual-Weyl module by its characteristic-zero semisimplification.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Import the integral induced representation and its base-change API from LP3.
Apply B0’s associated-bundle functor to M_dR and compare local equivariant functions.
Identify extensions through their toroidal charts and boundary ideal; preserve the left action order.
acceptance: The left translation is a representation and commutes with the right B law.

nodes.title: The Siegel weight dictionary
nodes.statement: For g=2 and integers a≥b, set ω(a,b)=Sym^(a−b)(E)⊗det(E)^b, E the rank-two Hodge bundle. Pilloni’s Ω^(k,r) is ω(k+r,r). In CG20’s Levi coordinates the natural coefficient is W_(a,b;−a−b); changing the central coordinate preserves the underlying bundle and changes its Hecke linearization. In BP26’s coordinates Lie(A) has weight ((0,…,−1);1) and ω_A weight ((1,0,…);−1). The dictionary must identify the actual multiplier characters rather than identify differently named central coordinates by notation.

proofSteps: Evaluate the standard, dual and determinant representations on the diagonal Levi.
Use the logarithmic sequence 0→W_(1,0;0)→H¹_dR→W_(0,−1;1)→0 and O(1)=W_(0,0;1).
Compare on a frame; record the change of central linearization separately from the underlying sheaf isomorphism.

nodes.title: Integral coherent cohomology complexes
nodes.statement: For a proper toroidal O-model X and finite locally free F, let C_can(F)=RΓ(X,F_can) and C_sub(F)=RΓ(X,F_sub) in D(O); their reductions are derived coefficient tensors. Retain the canonical arrow C_sub→C_can. Under proper flat finite-presentation and perfect-coefficient hypotheses these objects are perfect over O. They are not automatically perfect over a deck-group ring.

nodes.title: Coherent homology over a DVR
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with uniformizer ϖ, fraction field E, residue characteristic p, A_n=O/ϖ^n with n≥1, and Y/O smooth proper of pure relative dimension d. For finite locally free F define H_i(Y,F⊗A_n)=Hom_O(H^i(Y,F^∨⊗ω_(Y/O)⊗A_n),E/O). Deck transformations act contragrediently. The coefficient dual is Matlis dual over O; identifying it with Z_p-Pontryagin dual requires a chosen character and the inverse different.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Form the coherent dual coefficient F^∨⊗ω and take its cohomology.
Apply Hom_O(−,E/O), using injectivity over a DVR and inverse deck action.
Construct comparison maps under finite étale pullback by dualizing trace.
acceptance: The action convention must turn pullback on the dual coefficient into covariant homology.

nodes.title: Finite-coefficient Serre duality
nodes.statement: Under the preceding smooth proper relative-dimension-d assumptions, duality over A_n identifies H_i(Y,F⊗A_n) with H^(d−i)(Y_(A_n),F⊗A_n), using the self-duality A_n→Hom_O(A_n,E/O). Apply the chosen self-duality of the Artinian Gorenstein coefficient ring and exact Matlis duality.

nodes.title: The equivariant Čech model
nodes.statement: Let f:Y→X be a finite étale Galois cover of smooth proper O-schemes with finite abelian p-group Δ, and let F be finite locally free on X. Choose a finite affine cover of separated X; its inverse-image cover gives a bounded alternating Čech complex for f*F⊗A_n with its actual Δ action, computing RΓ(Y,f*F⊗A_n). Its terms may have infinite rank over A_n[Δ]. Refinements give the same derived object.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Pull back the affine cover; finite étale maps and finite intersections preserve affineness.
Apply affine quasi-coherent acyclicity and Čech comparison.
Write each coefficient term as N⊗_A B and preserve all deck operators in the differentials.
acceptance: The model is equivariant before passing to cohomology, and no finite-generation claim is made for its terms.

nodes.title: Étale Galois projectivity
nodes.statement: For a finite étale Galois cover f:Y→X with finite group Δ, f_*O_Y is locally projective as an O_X[Δ]-module. If X is flat over A, it is A[Δ]-flat. For a Δ-pulled-back finite locally free coefficient the same flatness holds. For an affine torsor in characteristic p with Δ a p-group, its coefficient module is free over k[Δ], possibly of infinite rank; local projectivity does not in general give a global integral normal basis over O_X[Δ].
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: After an étale trivialization of the torsor, the regular representation gives a free O_X[Δ]-module.
Descend finite projectivity and use flatness of the base algebra over A.
For the affine characteristic-p assertion use Nakajima’s theorem and the local Artinian structure of k[Δ], not averaging by |Δ|.
acceptance: Test a trivial torsor with p dividing |Δ|; the result must survive without dividing by |Δ|.

nodes.title: Perfect models for coherent cohomology and homology
nodes.statement: For the cover and coefficient of equivariant-cech, there is a bounded finite projective A_n[Δ]-complex representing RΓ(Y,f*F⊗A_n). Apply this to f*F^∨⊗ω_(Y/O) to obtain C_n^∨. Its A_n-linear derived dual, with inverse Δ action, gives C_n with H_i(C_n)=H_i(Y,f*F⊗A_n), after the Serre-dual coefficient is used on the cochain side. Choose the convention C_n^∨ represents RΓ(F^∨⊗ω), so C_n is its coefficient-dual chain model. Group-ring coefficient reduction means A_m[Δ]⊗^L_(A_n[Δ])C_n^∨, equivalently derived reduction of its termwise A_n-free model. Models and Hecke lifts are canonical only in the derived category or up to homotopy.

proofSteps: Bounded free Čech terms give finite Tor amplitude over the Noetherian ring A_n[Δ].

Take the imported finite-projective dual model and use evaluation to identify its chain homology.

nodes.title: Cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: For separated finite-type S-schemes C,X with (p₁,p₂):C→X×_S X proper, and coefficient complexes F,G on X, a cohomological correspondence is a morphism T:Lp₂*F→p₁!G in the coherent/discrete derived category when the indicated operations and boundedness exist. When p₁ is proper its adjoint is Rp₁*Lp₂*F→G; in the solid six-operation setting the general adjoint uses lower shriek (p₁)!, not unrestricted Rp₁*. The solid version uses the stable solid O-module category and its upper shriek; this enhancement is an explicit missing supplier, not an alternative definition of ordinary coherent cohomology.

nodes.title: Correspondences from a fundamental class
nodes.statement: Let C and X be S-schemes of the same pure relative dimension, p₁,p₂:C⇒X, with p₁ projectively embeddable and satisfying the SF.2 fundamental-class hypotheses. Equal dimensions alone do not supply the class. For finite locally free p₁ its adjoint is the algebra trace. Boundary twists use the reduced-relative-Cartier and inverse-image boundary hypotheses of A0/fundamental-class-boundary; its determinant route additionally retains the normal/smooth dense-open and relative normal-crossings hypotheses of P20 Lemma 4.2.4.1(1).

nodes.title: GAGA and the coherent tower
nodes.statement: For proper toroidal complex models, algebraic coherent cohomology agrees with analytic coherent cohomology in all degrees, naturally for Hecke pullback, trace, coefficient maps and boundary arrows. There is N(μ,levels) such that every parallel twist μ+t with t≥N has H^i_sub(X_k,ω_(μ+t))=0 for i>0. Consequently reduction H⁰_sub(O)→H⁰_sub(k) and the quotient map H⁰_sub(E)→H⁰_sub(E/O) are surjective, with their coefficient exact-sequence interpretation. No bound uniform over all levels is asserted.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Push subcanonical coefficients to the minimal model using relative vanishing.
Use Serre vanishing after ample Hodge twisting, and take the maximum bound over the fixed finite set of levels.
Use the ϖ-adic and E/O coefficient long exact sequences, proper finite cohomology and Nakayama to get the two surjections.
acceptance: Both surjections must be derived from H¹ vanishing; a bound depending only on μ while Q varies is not claimed.

nodes.title: The EO Cousin computation
nodes.statement: At hyperspecial p-level on the smooth Hilbert–Siegel toroidal model, filter by closures of Ekedahl–Oort strata of codimension at least i. For subcanonical locally free automorphic coefficients modulo pⁿ, n≥1, the Kempf Cousin resolution computes the sheaf, and its global-section complex computes RΓ once the following acyclicity is proved. The canonical-coefficient algebra action is obtained separately by coherent duality, not by assuming the same untwisted canonical Cousin acyclicity. Prove acyclicity using the affine stratum image on the minimal compactification, cofinal regular-sequence thickenings, Koszul resolutions and Lan relative vanishing. Affineness of the stratum itself is not assumed in place of this argument.

proofSteps: Import the EO geometric codimension, affine-image and regular-immersion results; their Hilbert–Siegel model owner is a recorded gap.
Apply the general Kempf resolution to the MCM coefficient and identify the support terms by cofinal Koszul thickenings.
Use relative vanishing over the affine minimal stratum image to prove the required term acyclicity.
acceptance: The cofinal thickenings and regular sequences are checked, rather than equating set-theoretic codimension with a chosen complete intersection.

nodes.title: Injecting the Cousin complex into the interior
nodes.statement: For the preceding EO filtration, restriction of every Cousin term of a subcanonical coefficient to the open Shimura variety is injective, provided the boundary equation is a non-zero-divisor on every relevant regular-sequence quotient. Verify this using that no component of the relevant EO stratum is contained in the boundary and the Cohen–Macaulay thickening argument. The omitted geometric verification is recorded as a gap. This is a termwise detection statement, not an assertion that global coherent cohomology injects into open cohomology in every degree.

Localize at the boundary equation and use the resulting injection in every term.
acceptance: Restriction of an arbitrary coherent cohomology group is not substituted for the termwise injection.

nodes.title: Integral prime-to-p Hecke relations at hyperspecial level
nodes.statement: For the BCGP21 Hilbert–Siegel models with p split completely in F and K_p=∏_(v|p)GSp₄(O_(F_v)), prime-to-p Hecke operators act through the abstract integral Hecke algebra on RΓ of canonical and subcanonical automorphic coefficients. nodes.title: Localized coherent perfect complexes
nodes.statement: Assume a commuting Hecke-algebra action on C_n^∨ has been supplied (for the integral geometric application use integral-hecke-relations, not merely the individual IC.3 operators). Let T_n be its finite A_n-algebra image in End_D(C_n^∨). For a maximal ideal m, its Artinian local-factor idempotent splits C_n^∨ into a perfect summand C_(n,m)^∨ and its complement, with H^i(C_(n,m)^∨)=H^i(C_n^∨)_m. The dual chain summand localizes at the transposed Hecke ideal, with character twists transported explicitly. This is not localization at an arbitrary prime by an idempotent over an arbitrary base.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Use finiteness of derived endomorphism groups of a perfect finite-coefficient complex to get finite T_n.
Apply the imported Artinian idempotent decomposition and perfect retract theorem.
Identify cohomology and transport the dual action via the transpose pairing.
acceptance: The localization projector is an endomorphism in the derived category and is represented up to homotopy.

nodes.title: Congruence localization of complex coherent cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a finite O-Hecke image T and an embedding of its characteristic-zero coefficient field into C. For a residual maximal ideal m, define M_(m,C) as the sum of the generalized characteristic-zero Hecke eigenspaces whose integral characters reduce to m after passing to a common finite coefficient extension. In degrees j=0,1, localized interior cohomology is exactly the multiplicity-counted cuspidal sum with the holomorphic (j=0) or generic (j=1) archimedean limit and the same finite level and residual congruence. Boundary vanishing identifies this with localized subcanonical cohomology. No large-weight lower bound on a is required for this conditional rational result.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Place interior cohomology between the injective cusp image and the L² relative-cohomology source.
Exclude nongeneral-type L² contributions with the residual Galois witness; purity makes the remaining archimedean factor essentially tempered, and Wallach makes the global representation cuspidal.
The same cuspidal sum bounds both sides. Use the full compact-group degree calculation and actual multiplicity spaces to identify degrees zero and one.
acceptance: The conditional conclusion includes a=2; do not replace it by the separate large-weight theorem.

nodes.title: Localized coherent cohomology and cuspidal representations
nodes.statement: Under BCGP21’s totally real hypotheses and non-Eisenstein localization, for i=0,1 there is a Hecke-equivariant injection from the multiplicity-counted sum of π_f^K into H^i_sub(X_C,ω_κ)_m, where π is cuspidal, congruent to m, holomorphic at real v with l_v>2 and nonholomorphic at exactly i places among those with l_v=2. For degree zero the holomorphic cusp dictionary gives equality. For degrees zero and one, the large-gap assumptions k_v−l_v>R and either l_v=2 or l_v>R give equality with the stated cuspidal sum. Multiplicity-free indexing additionally uses the conditional classification package; no unconditional multiplicity-one statement is claimed.

nodes.title: Conditional coherent dimension equality
nodes.statement: Assume the large-gap hypotheses of localized-cuspidal-decomposition and the conditional general-type packet pairing/multiplicity formula. Let l₀ be the number of real places with l_v=2. Then dim_C H¹_sub(X_C,ω_κ)_m=l₀·dim_C H⁰_sub(X_C,ω_κ)_m. Independently, over Q the conditional all-weight exhaustion and packet pairing give h¹=h⁰ for every a≥2 in weight (a,2), with no large-gap hypothesis, at neat prime-to-p level and non-Eisenstein localization. The factor l₀ counts permitted single archimedean changes within each packet with the same finite part.
hypotheses: The coefficient, geometric, level and normalization assumptions in the statement are part of the target; the conventions at the beginning of the reader apply.
proofSteps: Group the multiplicity-counted cuspidal summands by their finite part and global parameter.
Use the conditional packet formula to pair holomorphic with each permitted single generic archimedean change.
Multiply the equal finite-level dimensions by l₀ and sum over the residual congruence summand.
acceptance: If l₀=0 the formula predicts zero degree-one cohomology under the same large-weight and classification hypotheses.

gaps.detail: H90 Theorem 2.7 and Proposition 2.7.2, pp. 58–59, now verify the cusp/interior comparison directly, with the growth resolution in Theorem 2.4.4, p. 57.
